caption: "measles" — 50,000+ searches this week, up 1,000% today. Swipe for 10 things most people don't know about the disease America beat in 2000.

Why: Pennsylvania hit 792 cases across 39 counties on Monday and asked the CDC for help. Nationally, 3,471 cases by September 17, the most in three decades, above all of 2025. A regional commission rules in November on America's measles-free status.

What most people don't know: nine in ten unprotected people who share a home with a case catch it, and the virus lingers airborne for two hours. Two MMR doses protect 97 to 99%. Kindergarten coverage slipped from 95.2% to 92.4% since 2019.
Very simply put: measles-free since 2000; the verdict comes in November.

slides.headline: America beat measles in 2000. This year: *3,471 cases*.
slides.sub: 10 things most people don't know about the outbreak, searches up 1,000% today.
slides.image: A single glass vaccine vial standing on a bright white surface in clean clinical light, vial in the upper two thirds of the frame, lower third plain white, vivid, high contrast, photorealistic, no text, no labels

slides.headline: Pennsylvania: *792 cases* in 39 counties, and a call for help.
slides.sub: Its health secretary wrote to the CDC on Monday. The state recorded its first measles deaths in 35 years in August, both unvaccinated.
slides.image: A quiet Pennsylvania farm road with a white barn under a grey sky, barn in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain road, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: *3,471* US cases by September 17, more than all of 2025.
slides.sub: 2025 ended with 2,289, itself the worst year in decades. 89% of this year's cases were unvaccinated or of unknown status.
slides.image: Rows of small red dots pinned on a plain white map of the United States, map in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain white, photorealistic, no readable text

slides.headline: It started with *two imported cases* in Texas, in early 2025.
slides.sub: That outbreak killed two children. The chain has since reached 45 states.
slides.image: An empty airport arrivals hall with a long window and bright light, hall in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain polished floor, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: Nine in ten unprotected people in the same home *catch it*.
slides.sub: The virus stays in the air for up to two hours after an infected person leaves the room.
slides.image: Dust motes floating in a shaft of sunlight in an empty living room, light in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain wooden floor, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: It kills *1 to 3* of every 1,000 children who get it.
slides.sub: About 30% of cases have complications: pneumonia, ear infections, encephalitis. It can wipe immune memory for up to three years.
slides.image: An empty hospital bed with white sheets in a bright ward, bed in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain floor, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: Two MMR doses: *97 to 99%* protected.
slides.sub: One dose is about 95%. Herd immunity needs about 95% of the population covered.
slides.image: Two small adhesive bandages on a plain pale blue surface in soft light, bandages in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain blue, photorealistic, no text

slides.headline: Kindergarten coverage fell from 95.2% to *92.4%*.
slides.sub: From 2019 to the 2025-26 school year. Only 10 states still reach the 95% threshold.
slides.image: A row of small empty school chairs in a bright classroom, chairs in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain floor, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: *Canada* lost its measles-free status in 2025.
slides.sub: With 5,462 cases. The US, measles-free since 2000, gets its verdict from a regional commission in November.
slides.image: A red maple leaf frozen in clear ice on a plain white surface, leaf in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain white, photorealistic, no text

slides.headline: Very simply put: measles-free since 2000; the verdict comes in *November*.
